name: Kim Cheon-taek (comp.)
credit: A page of the 1728 Jinbon manuscript of the Cheonggu yeongeon (National Hangeul Museum scan, Wikimedia Commons) · Public domain. No portrait of Kim Cheon-taek exists.
bio: Kim Cheon-taek compiled the Cheonggu yeongeon (靑丘永言, 'Songs of the Blue Hills'), finished in 1728, the oldest surviving anthology of Korean sijo. He was himself a singer and poet of the commoner (yeohang) circle, known by the pen name Nampa (南坡), under which the book's commoner section carries songs of his own. His birth and death years are not documented in this edition, so 1728 stands here for the year of compilation.

The manuscript, known as the Jinbon, arranges nearly six hundred songs by the musical mode in which they were sung, then by poet: late Goryeo statesmen, the writers of Joseon, kings, commoner singers, gentlewomen such as the courtesan Hwang Jin, and many anonymous voices, closing with the long, unruly Manhoengcheongnyu songs. It carries a preface by Jeong Rae-gyo and a postface by Yi Jeong-seop, and the text is in Middle Korean, mixing hangul (with archaic letters) and hanja.
